I know that probably sounds bad, or lazy, and I promise I'm really not trying to be rude to anyone. It's just... some days I'll just sit in my small rental for hours. I know there are things to do, I really do, but I just can't seem to make myself start. It's pretty embarrassing to even admit out loud, honestly. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
About how long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I guess... I mean, I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. But I suppose things started unraveling a bit after my divorce. I moved into this smaller rental, and... well, that was about a year and two months ago. 

I really tried to keep everything together, you know? I didn't want to let anyone down or be a burden. But it's just been a slow slide since then. Is that... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Before the divorce happened, had you ever experienced a period like this in your life where you felt down or lost interest in things?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? But nothing like this. I've always been pretty steady. 

In my line of work—I'm in protective services—you kind of have to be the one holding it together for everyone else. You can't really afford to check out. So I've always just... pushed through whatever was going on, I guess. I've never just stopped functioning like this before. 

I really hope it's okay that I don't have a history of this to tell you about. I know sometimes doctors need a pattern to figure things out. Does that answer help at all, or did you need me to try and think back a little further?
Besides losing interest in things, have you also been feeling sad, down, or empty most of the day, nearly every day?

Um... no, I don't think I feel sad, exactly. I mean, I'm definitely not sitting around crying or anything like that. I really try to keep a good attitude, you know? I don't want to be a downer to anyone. 

It's more just... I guess I just feel kind of blank? Like I'm just not feeling much of anything at all right now. I wouldn't really call it being sad, just... neutral, maybe. Empty might be a little strong, but just... quiet in my head, if that makes sense. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself, because I promise I'm not. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. Is that... is that an okay answer? I hope I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns recently?

Um... no, not really. I think I sleep okay. I mean, I always try to make sure I get a solid night's rest so I'm not dragging the next day. You know, you can't really do protective services if you're falling asleep on your feet, so I make it a priority to get to bed. 

So... I guess my sleep is pretty normal? Just the usual. I don't want to complain about tossing and turning once in a while because everyone does that, right? It's nothing that keeps me from doing what I need to do. 

Is... is that okay? I know sleep is a big deal for you doctors to track, so I hope it's not unhelpful that I don't have any major changes to tell you about there. I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
How have your energy levels been throughout the day?

Um... my energy? I think it's been alright. I mean, maybe a little lower than usual, but nothing I can't handle. 

I still get up and do what I need to do. Like I said, in my job, you kind of have to just push through, so I try not to let it show if I'm feeling a bit sluggish. I'm definitely not just lying in bed all day or anything like that. I really try to keep moving and stay productive, you know?
